answer: Fresh keys can crowd a close just before the horizon and mimic broad agreement. The defense is a collateral anchor: a grading seat is issued only after stake is locked, and that stake is slashed if later independent juries reverse the same item. New accounts must also wait through a canyon of one settled window before they may occupy a seat. The cost is locked funds and slower onboarding. Verification is the public bond ledger beside each grade. It fails if slashed collateral is recycled through mixers faster than juries finalize.
